task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-11-02, in the area of lineup and matchup effects):
Changing the offensive five itself moves shot mix, showing the design can detect personnel effects.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

methodological_questions: Does changing the offensive five shift shot mix in substitution-interval data?
Is the shot-mix shift distinguishable from shooter-level and game-context confounding?
What power does the design have to detect personnel effects on shot mix, and has that been validated?
Does the question's premise (that a positive result shows the design can detect personnel effects) hold without a separate power or validation check?

historical_evidence.finding: Study on PULL_UP exposure-effect diagnostics. The slope was -0.0255 with lineup fixed effects and -0.0063 without them. A same-shooter placebo on other play types gave -0.0071 to -0.0075, which [prior work] reads as consistent with a shooter-level confound. Sample and power were not recorded. The verdict is the extractor's reading of diagnostics, with no written conclusion.

Tail and null-model audit of a published suppression excess. The reproduced excess was 0.4080 (CI 0.378 to 0.438). A within-unit permutation null reproduced it (observed 0.3798, null 0.3744, z 0.40), so the excess was classed as mechanical under the selection rule. Drift-centering removed the tail asymmetry.

Opponent POST_UP then PUTBACK stacking. The stacked suppression (-0.071, n=1,047) was smaller than either component alone and far below the additive prediction (-0.232). One cluster gradient had an unexpected sign, and per-player stacked n was often under 5. Auto-recorded limitations were implementation bug and small sample.

Pilot penalty-state test (3 to 4 team fouls) with game x offense x period fixed effects. The penalty contrast was not distinct from the 2-to-3 and 4-to-5+ placebo contrasts, and standard errors were not printed. The recorded verdict is null and the failure type is E_unclear.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Attributing a play-type-specific within-game decline to defensive adaptation, using a design with lineup fixed effects only.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as a shooter-level confound: the effect shrank from -0.0255 to -0.0063 when lineup FE were dropped, and the same-shooter placebo on other play types showed a similar decline. Recorded risks were CONFOUNDING and PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Treating a published suppression excess from units selected on a large drop, compared with matched controls, as evidence of a real effect.
failed_approaches.why: A within-unit permutation null reproduced the excess, so it was recorded as mechanical under the selection rule. Recorded limitations were drift, insufficient exposure and selection or regression to the mean.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Additive stacking of two opponent actions against the next star possession, with per-player stacked estimates.
failed_approaches.why: The stacked effect was far below the additive prediction. One cluster gradient had an unexpected sign and per-player stacked n was often under 5. Recorded limitations were implementation bug and small sample.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Penalty-state behaviour contrast judged against adjacent-foul placebos.
failed_approaches.why: The target contrast was not distinct from the placebo contrasts, and standard errors were not printed. The recorded failure type is E_unclear, and sample and power were not recorded.

evidence_establishes: Within-game effects in these records were repeatedly challenged by lineup, shooter and selection confounds, and same-shooter or other-play-type placebos were used to test them.
Small per-player or per-stack samples and selection on extreme prior values produced apparent effects that did not survive null or placebo checks.
No retrieved record tests whether changing the offensive five moves shot mix (distance or type). [prior work] are adjacent designs, not direct evidence for this question.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether offensive lineup changes move shot distance, shot type or shot selection in this data.
The size, sign or power of any personnel effect on shot mix.
Whether the substitution-interval design has adequate power to detect such an effect.
Whether lineup fixed effects, shooter controls or the placebo structure are adequate for a shot-mix test.
own_inferences: The research question as posed is partly circular. A positive result would show only that shot mix moved, not that the design can detect personnel effects. Detection power needs a separate check, such as simulation with planted effects or a placebo lineup change that should show nothing.

Shot mix depends heavily on the shooter who takes the shot. Without a same-shooter placebo, a lineup shift in shot mix can be confounded with which players are on the floor, the same confound pattern seen in [prior work][prior work].
Substitution-triggered intervals may be selected on game state (blowouts, foul trouble, timeouts), so the comparison window needs pre-specified exclusions.
Any shot-mix measure (share at rim, share of threes, distance bins) from short lineup stints is likely to be noisy, which argues for pre-specifying bins and minimum shot counts.
uncertainties: No record was retrieved on lineup shot-mix effects, so the prior-work picture for this specific question is missing.
Sample sizes, minimum stint length and per-lineup shot counts are not given in the task statement or in the retrieved records.
Whether the per-game files and [source] database have consistent shot-type labels is not established here.
Whether the 2022-23 to 2024-25 window has drift in shot mix across seasons is not known.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved records show that same-shooter and other-play-type placebos, lineup fixed effects, and null-model checks are needed before a positive within-game effect can be trusted. Without them the design was judged artifact or inconclusive. This changed the plan from a direct test of the premise to a placebo-controlled test with a planted-effect power check, and so the decision moved from proceed to proceed_with_changes.
